correctness.rationale: For fixed nonnegative integer j, uniform Hankel asymptotics at q near 4 split the common mean 3/(pi²(q-4)) from the oscillatory difference, which has mean zero between consecutive orders and converges conditionally when q↓4. Using (r J_{j-1}J_j)'=r(J_{j-1}²-J_j²) and Bessel recurrences reduces the adjacent fourth-power difference to 2[j² T_j-(j-1)² T_{j-1}], T_j=integral J_j^4/r. Neumann’s product identity plus regularized Frullani–Bessel angular logarithmic kernel evaluates T_j=(j² pi²)^-1 sum_{ell<=j}(2ell-1)^-1, hence adjacent limit 2/(pi²(2j-1)). Telescoping gives arbitrary fixed m<n and mean-value expansion of u^(2/q) gives the sqrt(q-4) coefficient. Boundary terms at 0 and infinity need fixed j and conditional integration, explicitly respected. Independent SciPy radial integrations for j=1..3 up to R=2500 matched exact T_j within around 1.2e-8, supporting but not proving tails.
